newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai officials seek to allay anthrax fears.
newsitem.headline: Thai officials seek to allay anthrax fears.

text.p: Thai authorities on Monday said an anthrax outbreak reported last week among cattle in a predominantly Moslem area on the outskirts of Bangkok was now under control.
They also ruled out newspaper reports that one man out of a group of 12 who had become infected after eating anthrax-infected beef had died from the disease.
"Doctors who examined the body found that the man had died of heart failure," said Thanee Yuthasaunthorn, the head of northern Suan Luang district where the outbreak occurred.
Anthrax is an infectious disease of wild and domesticated animals, especially cattle and sheep, which causes profuse bleeding and can be transmitted to people.
It causes skin infection, diarrhoea and fever among other symptoms and can be fatal if it infects the brain, medical officials said.
Medical teams had been sent to the area and the outbreak was now under control, Thanee told Reuters.
